csv_project_name: AE for UNLV CCLB 3 Mechanical System Replace
csv_scope_of_work: UNLV is encountering substantial operational challenges regarding the legacy mechanical infrastructure within Campus Lab Building 3 (CLB3). Critical issues include the inability to sustain stable environmental temperatures, excessive requirements for ongoing maintenance and repair of mechanical units, and persistent dust infiltration in Research Laboratories likely caused by compromised ductwork. Furthermore, the current system lacks adequate automated controls. To address these concerns, UNLV contracted Turpin & Rattan Engineering Inc. (TREI) to perform a comprehensive facility assessment. This engagement encompassed a rigorous evaluation of existing site conditions, an analysis of historical Testing, Adjusting, and Balancing (TAB) documentation, and a high-level review of the central plant. TREI conducted visual inspections of accessible major equipment, resulting in a detailed report (Exhibit B) outlining recommended improvements and technical strategies for the modernization or replacement of the mechanical systems. UNLV is seeking an experienced and qualified Prime Architect to provide Architectural Design Services which include code analysis, fire protection, as well as services from Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing ( MEP ) Engineers, and Structural Engineers for the mechanical system replacement in building CLB3 including but not limited to new Air Handler's, Building Automation System design, air distribution and energy code review. SCOPE: Phase I: Design through Construction Documents. 1. Provide design services for the mechanical system replacement in building CLB3 which contains a wide range of Labs such as chemistry, biochemistry, engineering, and public health. The scope will include but not limited to: a. Full replacement of Air Handler-18 employing a variable air volume control strategy with pressure sensors in labs to ensure negatively pressurized spaces and code compliance. See Exhibit B and ensure the firm s MEP consultants have thoroughly reviewed the exhibit. b. Replacement of existing air handling units Air Handler-16 and Air Handler-13 in mechanical room 117. See Exhibit B. c. Replacement of miscellaneous equipment including but not limited to water pumps. See Exhibit B. d. Tie the new system into the existing central plant as required. See Exhibit B. e. Design new Building Automation System (BAS). Heating Ventilation and Air Conditioning BAS for HVAC including sensors, controllers, output devices, communication protocols and a user interface/dashboard. Also required is the physical integration of hardware, software configuration, and testing. Replace existing T-stats and sensor devices throughout the building. Possibly rezone the air distribution. f. Replace existing duct socks with new metal ductwork and specify all existing ducts to be cleaned and sealed. g. Replace existing louvers, diffusers and grills typical. h. Designer to specify that all abandoned existing equipment shall be removed & discarded. i. Designer to specify the removal of the existing pneumatic controls. j. Existing fume hood system shall be upgraded and equipped with new high-performance venturi air valves (i.e. Phoenix valves or equal.) k. The shaft or interstitial space behind the fume hoods are to be evaluated. Recommendations shall be incorporated into the design drawings to prevent dust infiltration without compromising the integrity of the fume hood or mechanical system. l. Design for Fire Alarm (FA) devices to be integrated with the new mechanical system. m. Modernize the existing network system to accommodate the new BAS. n. Coordinate with an Owner's Commissioning Agent. o. Specify a final Testing, Adjusting, and Balancing (TAB) report for proper overall balancing. p. Code Review including Energy Code. 2. Engage required consultants to provide complete design services. Your Prime Architect s proposal shall include a list of all subconsultants. 3. Engage a Cost Estimator to provide cost estimates at the end of each design phase - Preliminary Design, Design Development and Construction Documents (PD, DD & CD). Note: UNLV may engage a Construction Manager At Risk (CMAR) for this project. CMAR duties shall include but not limited to pre-construction services such as, the development of schedules, preparation of construction cost models/estimates, field verification of all conditions, etc., to be managed by the CMAR. 4. Meet weekly with UNLV Planning & Construction and the CMAR (if applicable) teams to demonstrate progress. 5. Coordination of the design drawings between Prime Architect & consultants for the renovation. 6. Preparation of construction drawings and specifications describing design for cost estimating. 7. Respond to CMAR s requests for information (if applicable). 8. Provide CAD dwg files of final design drawings for the Prime Architect and consultants drawings. 9. The Prime Architect shall be responsible for field measuring the existing space to confirm dimensions. 10.Establish a design schedule based on the attached preliminary project schedule. 11.Preparation of construction drawings and specifications describing design and construction work for filing with the State Public Works Department (S.P.W.D.) and for bidding to prospective contractors. SCOPE: Phase II: Filing, Bidding, Construction Administration and Closeout 12.S.P.W.D. applications and design drawings for Architectural & Engineering work shall be signed & sealed by Prime Architect and consultants respective offices. Submission to S.P.W.D. by UNLV Planning & Construction (UNLV P&C) 13.In conjunction with the required controlled inspections, the Prime Architect & Engineers shall periodically inspect the construction work once construction is under way. A written report of those inspections shall be submitted to UNLV P&C. 14.Provide UNLV P&C with Drawings & Specifications in PDF format for distribution of bid package to prospective bidders 15.Respond to bidders requests for information and provide assistance with evaluation of bidders proposals. 16.Revise the design drawings as a result of the contractor bidding process and the S.P.W.D. review, as Issued for Construction drawings. 17.Provide construction administration oversite, including review of submittals, attendance at construction meetings, periodic site inspections, evaluation of contractor change-orders proposals, preparation of clarification sketches as needed, punch list of completed work, and review of contractor s closeout documents.

Scope includes full replacement of Air Handler-18 with variable air volume control and lab pressure sensors for negative pressurization, replacement of Air Handler-16 and Air Handler-13 in mechanical room 117, replacement of miscellaneous equipment including water pumps, integration with the existing central plant, design of a new HVAC building automation system, replacement of thermostats and sensors, possible rezoning of air distribution, replacement of duct socks with metal ductwork, duct cleaning and sealing, replacement of louvers/diffusers/grilles, removal of abandoned equipment and pneumatic controls, upgrade of fume hood systems with high-performance venturi air valves, evaluation of shaft/interstitial spaces behind fume hoods to prevent dust infiltration, fire alarm integration, network modernization for BAS, commissioning coordination, TAB reporting, and code and energy code review.
services: Prime architect-led architectural and engineering design services including code analysis, fire protection, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and structural engineering; Phase I design through construction documents; Phase II filing, bidding, construction administration, inspections, bid support, submittal review, change order evaluation, punch list, and closeout. Cost estimating and consultant coordination are also required.
relevance_explanation:
- Primarily a building mechanical systems replacement project focused on MEP and BAS modernization.
- Structural engineering is only a minor supporting discipline, with no significant structural scope described.
- Project does not involve bridges, long-span roofs, special structures, stadiums, or architecturally demanding building structures.
- Tender seeks a prime architect with broad consultant team rather than a specialist structural concept role.
- Construction budget is modest and technical complexity is concentrated in HVAC/lab systems, which is outside sbp's core focus.
